The U.S. Embassy in Kuwait urges U.S. citizens in Kuwait to shelter in place, review security plans in the event of an attack, and to stay alert in case of additional future attacks. U.S. Embassy personnel are sheltering in place.
Actions to take:
- If you hear a loud explosion, or if sirens are activated, immediately seek cover.
- If in a home or building, go to the lowest level of the structure with the fewest exterior walls, windows, and openings; close any doors and sit near an interior wall, away from any windows or openings.
- If you are outdoors, immediately seek cover in a hardened structure; if that is not possible, lie down and cover your head with your hands.
- Be aware that even if the incoming missile or drone is intercepted, falling debris represents a significant risk.
- After the attack, stay away from any debris, and monitor major news outlets for official guidance.

🚨 NEW | U.S. F-15E crashes in Kuwait — two American crew members successfully eject

A U.S. Air Force F-15E Strike Eagle crashed in Al Jahra, west of Kuwait City, on March 2. Both the pilot and weapons systems officer successfully ejected and survived. Video circulating online shows local residents assisting one of the crew in a civilian truck.

The crash site in Al Jahra was geolocated by OSINT researcher Christiaan Triebert. Debris reportedly fell inside the Mina Al Ahmadi refinery complex, injuring at least two refinery workers.

No official cause has been confirmed.

➤ Some reports suggest possible friendly fire from a Patriot air defense battery during heightened alert.
➤ Iranian state-linked media claims the aircraft was shot down.
➤ Mechanical failure is also possible, with online reports noting footage showed smoke and one engine on fire before the jet spiraled down.

More details 👇

🚨 35 killed in Pakistan amid protests over U.S.-Israeli attacks on Iran

At least 35 civilians have been killed across Pakistan after protests erupted denouncing the joint U.S.–Israeli strikes on neighboring Iran that also killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. 

The death toll was 16 people killed in Karachi, 7 in Gilgit, 6 in Skardu, and 6 in Islamabad – according to Jamhoor Media journalist @AlifyaSohail. Al Jazeera and other outlets have separately confirmed deadly clashes nationwide with slightly different death tolls.

➤ Karachi: At least 16 killed, 34+ injured after protesters breached the outer wall of the U.S. Consulate. Reports say Marine Security Guards and local police opened fire after parts of the compound and nearby police posts were set ablaze.

➤ Gilgit (7 dead): Clashes with police turned deadly amid large anti-U.S. demonstrations in the city.

➤ Skardu (6 dead): Protesters torched a UN office (UNDP/UNMOGIP complex), with multiple fatalities reported during confrontations with security forces.

➤ Islamabad (6 dead): Security forces used tear gas and live ammunition to block roughly 4,000 protesters from entering the heavily guarded Diplomatic Enclave near the U.S. Embassy.

There are unconfirmed reports of an information clampdown, with hospitals allegedly restricted from releasing full casualty data. The U.S. Embassy has issued a high-level security alert as protests continue in multiple cities.
